lines.text: Companies pay a frontier model for every coding call, even FizzBuzz. CHIMERA answers each call at the cheapest place that gets it right.
This take is live, on our own GPU. The whole app is one page. Hold W. The gates open, then the great door.

I ask the Count a question. The call climbs a ladder: our shared cache first, then our own 30B, then the big 763B. The cache has not seen this one. So our 30B answers, on our A6000, in under a second. No token bill.
The same question again. The cache answers in a tenth of a second. Zero tokens. No model was called.
FizzBuzz. Our 30B writes it in about one and a half seconds. All 163 tokens stay off the 763B.

Now a hard design task. The 30B tries first, but it is not sure: 0.87, under our 0.95 bar. So the call climbs to the 763B. Here is a loss. With the climb it took 9 seconds. The 763B alone took 5, at about the same cost.

Here is the bill for a month of coding calls. With 3 in 10 calls being repeats, we spend 62 to 87 percent less than GPT-5.5 alone. Now the loss. Against the cheap 763B, at 100 thousand calls a day, we cost 607 percent more.
We built this with Kiro. Seven steering files, seven specs, six hooks, four custom agents, MCP tools and a Power. Property tests from the specs found four real bugs. All four are fixed.
Stop paying a frontier model for FizzBuzz. We prove it with tests.
On our own A6000, 763B calls fell 70.7 percent, with zero wrong answers from the cache. We passed 292 of 301 coding tasks. The 763B alone passed 286. But a first pass is slower.
